transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what has been going on that made you decide to seek help today?

Well… I came in because my mind just doesn’t seem to hold onto things anymore. Like, I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program — I’ve done that kind of thing for years, you know, little reminders, schedules, numbers for supplies — and suddenly the words and numbers just scatter on me. Something I could do in my sleep before, and now I’m staring at the page like it’s moving away from me.

Can you tell me more about these memory problems? For example, how long have you been experiencing this, and have you noticed any other areas of your life where you’re having trouble remembering things?

It’s been… I don’t know, it feels like lately my head just won’t keep hold of things. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program — I’ve done that sort of thing for years — and suddenly the numbers and words just scatter. Like I’m reaching for them and they slip off somewhere.

It’s embarrassing, really. I used to make supply lists, little schedules, reminders for the kids, and now I just stare at the paper. And then I start thinking about the old workshop space, how we used to keep everything in those blue bins, and I can picture the bins clear as day, but the thing I’m supposed to write down right then… it just won’t come together.
Have you noticed any other changes in your thinking or ability to handle everyday tasks, like keeping track of dates, managing money, or following instructions?

Mostly with writing things down, I guess. I mean, you ask about dates and money and instructions, and… I don’t know, it all feels tied to the same thing, like my mind won’t hold still long enough.

I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program — something I used to do without even thinking — and then the numbers and words just scatter on me. It’s like I know what I’m trying to say, but when I go to put it down, it won’t line up. And then I get sidetracked thinking about how I used to keep everything organized there, the kids coming in after school, the little supply lists… but the actual note in front of me just doesn’t come together.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak or write, even if you know what you mean?

Yes… I think that’s it, or part of it. I know what I mean in my head, but when I go to say it or write it down, the right words just don’t stay put. Especially writing — I’ll sit down to make a simple note for the youth maker program, something I used to do without even thinking, and the numbers and words sort of scatter on me.

It’s strange because I can remember the room, the tables, where we kept things, all of that… but the actual words I need right then, they just slip away.
Have you ever had trouble recognizing familiar people, common objects, or places you know well, like forgetting what a pen is used for or not recognizing your own home?

No, I don’t think so… not like that. I know what a pen is, I know my house when I’m there. People too, mostly — I mean, faces can catch me off guard if I’m tired, but I don’t think I’ve been looking at my own kitchen wondering where I am or anything.

It’s more… well, I shouldn’t get off track, but places have so many memories tied to them. Like the old program room, I can see it clear as anything — the tables, the bins, all that. So no, I haven’t noticed that kind of not-recognizing.
Have you ever experienced things that others don’t seem to see, hear, or feel — like hearing voices when no one is around, or believing something is happening that others don’t understand?

I don’t think so… not in the way you mean. I mean, I’m alone a lot, so sometimes the house makes noises, or I’ll think I heard something and then it’s just the refrigerator or the pipes. Houses do that, especially older ones — my father used to say every house has its own little language, which sounds silly now.

But voices, like someone talking to me when nobody’s there… no, I don’t think I’ve had that. And I don’t think there’s something happening that other people can’t see. Mostly I just get caught up in my own thoughts and then I lose track of what we were talking about.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yes… yes, most days. I wake up and there’s this heavy, hollow feeling right here in my chest, like something’s been scooped out but also weighing me down, if that makes sense.

And my wife will be kind to me — she is kind, she’ll say something gentle or ask if I want coffee — and I hear her, I know she means well, but it feels like I’m sitting at the bottom of a well. Like she’s far above me somewhere and I can’t quite get back up to where people are.

I used to… well, I used to enjoy things more, but it’s hard to explain without rambling. It’s mostly that sadness, that heaviness, being there when I wake up and then it just sort of stays.
Have there been times when you felt unusually upbeat, overly energetic, or irritable for several days, where you needed less sleep or felt like your thoughts were racing?

I don’t think so… I mean, I’ve had days where I’m restless or cross, sure, but not “upbeat” exactly. That word almost sounds like another person.

Less sleep… well, sleep gets strange when you’re older anyway, doesn’t it? My father used to be up at five every morning, puttering around with the kettle, and I used to think that was discipline, but maybe he just couldn’t sleep. I suppose I get off track.

No, I can’t really say I’ve had several days where I felt full of energy or like everything was racing in a good way. Mostly if my thoughts run, it doesn’t feel like energy so much as… well, I’m not sure that’s what you’re asking.
Have you had any trouble with things like judging distances, knowing which direction to turn, or handling situations that require planning several steps ahead?

I’m not sure about distances or directions exactly… I don’t drive much these days, so it’s hard to say. But planning things, yes, I think that’s part of why I came in.

My mind just won’t seem to hold onto things anymore. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program — something I used to be able to do almost in my sleep, you know, just a few lines and maybe some numbers — and then the words and numbers sort of scatter on me. I’ll look at the page and lose the thread of what I meant to put down.

It’s embarrassing, really. I used to be good at that sort of thing. Well… good enough, anyway.
Have you had increasing difficulty organizing tasks, making decisions, or solving problems, such as planning an event or managing your schedule for the youth maker program?

Yes… that’s really why I came in, I think. My mind just won’t hold onto things the way it used to.

I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program — just a small thing, something I used to do almost without thinking — and then the numbers and words sort of scatter on me. I look at the page and lose track of what I was trying to say.

It’s funny, I used to tell the kids to measure twice and cut once, you know, keep things in order… and now I can’t seem to keep a few lines straight. It’s… frustrating.
